opportunities.title: Separate Microsoft flow ownership from ID-token identity admission
opportunities.problem: MSAL 1.37.0 decodes ID-token claims but does not independently verify the JWS signature, contradicting the parent ownership contract.

options.security: Missing independent signature and rollover admission property.
options.performance: Lowest local CPU and metadata traffic.
options.memory: No second metadata or key cache.
options.reliability: Couples identity evidence to successful token-endpoint transport.
options.operability: Few components, but an unsafe and misleading ownership claim.

options.security: Independent RS256 signature and OIDC claim verification with no fallback.
options.performance: One local verification; metadata and keys are cached and refreshed only as bounded.
options.memory: One bounded Authlib metadata and JWK cache.
options.reliability: One library-owned refresh on unknown kid, then fail closed.
options.operability: Two maintained components with an explicit health and error seam.
options.migration: Small future adapter change while preserving MSAL flow ownership.

options.security: One coherent OIDC component could own both protocol and verification.
options.reliability: Mature client behavior, but entirely new flow integration.
options.migration: Replaces the selected MSAL path and reopens all flow evidence.

options.security: Requires bespoke discovery, algorithm, cache and rollover correctness.
options.performance: Could be lean but needs careful concurrency and refresh controls.
options.memory: Custom cache size and lifetime must be implemented.
options.reliability: Highest rollover, outage and stampede edge-case burden.
options.operability: EMR4 permanently owns security-sensitive verifier machinery.
options.migration: Moderate initial code and high ongoing maintenance.
